title: How he learned piano: picking it up by following the bands
summary: He took only brief lessons late, learned by hanging around with the bands, and describes the heavy chordal complement.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well, I was going to ask in the very beginning about if you ever had any lessons on the piano. You said that Rene and people helped you some. Oh, yeah. Did you ever take lessons on the piano with a book and a picture?
Yeah, I took lessons in first grade and second grade.
Well, I took it lately, you know.
Oh, and just in late, late, not when you were a little boy.
I was just a jazz man.

Just picked it up. Just picked it up like this. They went on and played and hang around them until I learned. And went on and played different jazz with them. Well, first time, you know, you get cold feet and just kept on until I learned. Sure. But sometime I'd go there and the pieces I could play, well, they'd play for me to catch on and that's how I come on. So that's how I got to learn. And Raffaella and them, I liked it and everywhere they'd go, I'd go. Everywhere I'd know they got to dance, I'd run behind them until I learned how to play.
Do you remember any of them?

I made a lot of money at it because, you know, me enjoying the time because I was getting the money and they was helping me out. I played pretty good at that time, you know, the jazz. But now the music has changed so you got to try to follow the crowd now, you know. Play the move. It's not complicated now as it's been done because the music was so hard then, you see. Of course you didn't have to do but complement and the way you complement then was different than when you complement now. Because the banjo was hitting. See that was the complement and you all you had to do is hit with the banjo then. So just hit cards the same way you would.

Make cards like that but now they make cards. Boom, boom, boom, boom. Boom, boom, boom. That's the kind of card now. But them time you make. Like that. It's playing cards. It's playing cards. Hit like you.
It's playing cards. Like your plug and something at that time, you see. And that's what they wanted, the chords, the heavy chords.
